关注领域

领域涵盖内容
AI 芯片与硬件GPU/NPU/TPU 等 AI 芯片的设计与架构；AI 服务器、数据中心硬件；芯片互联（NVLink/InfiniBand/PCIe）；NVIDIA/AMD/Intel/国产芯片产品动态与技术评测
AI 芯片软件栈AI 芯片配套软件生态，包括 CUDA/ROCm/XLA/OneAPI 等编程框架；cuDNN/cuBLAS 等算子库；AI 编译器（TVM/Triton/XLA）；Kernel 开发与优化；芯片软件适配与移植；软硬件协同优化
模型推理与部署推理加速框架（vLLM/SGLang/TensorRT-LLM/llama.cpp）；量化技术（GPTQ/AWQ/FP8/INT4）；推理 serving 架构；批处理与调度优化；边缘/端侧部署；推理性能显著提升的技术创新
模型训练与微调预训练技术与数据工程；SFT/RLHF/DPO 等对齐方法；分布式训练（Megatron-LM/DeepSpeed/FSDP）；训练效率优化；参数高效微调（LoRA/QLoRA）；训练基础设施
AI 开发框架与工具提升模型开发或应用构建效率的框架与工具（LangChain/LlamaIndex/Transformers等）；性能 Profiling 与调试工具；Benchmark 测评框架；显著提升易用性或开发效率的创新工具
大模型技术与应用基础大模型架构创新（Transformer 变体、MoE、SSM 等）；新模型发布与能力评测；多模态模型；模型优缺点分析与对比；大模型在各行业的落地应用；权威趋势预测与技术综述

训练微调预训练、SFT、RLHF、DPO、分布式训练、数据集构建、参数高效微调
性能优化系统级性能优化：算子/Kernel优化、内存优化、并行策略、CUDA/Triton优化、吞吐量与延迟改善
芯片软件栈AI芯片配套软件：CUDA/ROCm/XLA、编译器、算子库、Kernel开发、芯片软件适配与移植
AI芯片硬件GPU/NPU/TPU芯片架构与产品、AI数据中心硬件、芯片互联技术、芯片产品发布与评测
开发工具AI应用开发框架、SDK、Agent框架、RAG工具链、Profiling与调试工具

抓取策略：分类配额

每天 UTC 07:00（北京 15:00）自动抓取，每次最多 200 篇。不是简单按时间倒序——arXiv 每天数百篇会挤掉其他来源，因此按分类配额： · 优先抓全部 lab / tools / chip / newsletter / hackernews（每类上限 100，实际通常 <30） · 剩余配额给 arXiv（通常 140-150 篇） 保证 AI 公司官博、NVIDIA、PyTorch 等高价值来源不被海量论文挤掉。

相关度评分细则（DeepSeek 评分主体)

【核心收录主线 — AI 芯片硬件与软件栈强相关】 本资讯主要服务于 AI 芯片硬件与软件栈开发者， 最高优先级是判断文章对该群体的工程价值。 凡满足以下四类任一条件，视为强相关（评分区间 80–95）；多类同时满足取上限。 ① AI 芯片硬件特性 → 功耗 / 性能 / 延迟优化 - 新硬件架构、内存层级、互联拓扑（NVLink / InfiniBand / UB / PCIe）、新型计算单元 - 实测能效比、算力利用率（MFU/HFU）、显存带宽与延迟瓶颈分析 - 数据中心 / 推理集群级硬件优化 - GPU / NPU / TPU / ASIC 新品发布、实测性能、对比评测 - 国产 / 国际 AI 芯片对比、行业格局变化 ② 算法 / 算子性能优化 → 可下沉到软件栈直接带来收益 - 新算子、kernel 优化、内存访问模式、流水线编排 - 并行策略（TP / PP / EP / SP / CP / Ulysses）的具体实现与实测加速 - 量化（GPTQ / AWQ / FP8 / FP6 / INT4）、稀疏化在具体硬件上的加速数据 - 推理优化（continuous batching、PagedAttention、KV cache 压缩、speculative decoding） - 训练优化（gradient accumulation、activation checkpoint、ZeRO、混合精度） ③ 热门软件栈 / 工具 / 组件 / 新特性 → 需要 AI 芯片适配以满足兼容性 - 推理框架（vLLM、SGLang、TensorRT-LLM、llama.cpp、MLC-LLM）新版本 / 新特性 - 训练框架（Megatron-LM、Megatron-Core、DeepSpeed、FSDP、TorchTitan、ColossalAI）更新 - 编译器栈（Triton、XLA、TVM、MLIR、Mojo、Hidet）新特性 - 主流模型新发布且对推理栈有新需求（新 attention 变体、新量化格式、新数据类型） - 国产芯片需要适配的主流软件特性、生态进展 ④ SOTA 算法 / 算子 / 软件库 → 对芯片适配优化有参考价值 - SOTA attention 实现（FlashAttention 系列、Ring / Tree / Star Attention、Native Sparse Attention） - 高性能算子库（FlashInfer、CUTLASS、xformers、cuDNN、ThunderKittens 等的重要更新） - 主流框架的 reference 高性能内核 - SOTA 量化 / 稀疏化方法及其 reference 实现 【中等相关 — 65–80 分】 - 大模型新发布、能力评测、产品动态（缺乏芯片 / 软件栈层面的工程深度） - AI 公司动态、融资、组织调整（限重大事件） - 一般性研究综述、宏观趋势预测 【弱相关 / 周边 — 50–65 分】 - 应用层产品演示、行业用例（无底层技术细节） - 与底层硬件 / 软件栈无直接关联的 AI 研究 【明确排除，直接给分 ≤ 30】 - 非 AI 领域科技新闻（手机、电动车、区块链、量子计算等） - 纯商业 / 财经 / 政治新闻（融资除非涉及 AI 核心公司且金额重大） - AI 作为噱头的泛应用报道（AI 写作工具、AI 客服等边缘应用） - 传统 CV / NLP 小模型任务（与大模型 / 芯片无关） - X 平台上的个人生活、时事评论、非 AI 话题发言（即使来自知名人物） 【来源权威性辅助】在内容符合主线时叠加（+5~+15）： - 顶级 AI 公司官方博客：OpenAI、Anthropic、Google Research、DeepMind、NVIDIA、Meta AI - 行业领袖 X 发文（内容涉及 AI 技术 / 产品 / 趋势）：Karpathy、LeCun、Sam Altman、Dario Amodei、Demis Hassabis 等 - 顶级机构论文：Google / Meta / Microsoft / OpenAI / Anthropic / NVIDIA 及 MIT / Stanford / CMU / Berkeley 【arXiv 严格筛选】须满足任一项才能 ≥ 70 分： 1. 直接服务于推理 / 训练 / 芯片工程优化（对应主线 ②③④） 2. 顶级机构 + SOTA 声称且有具体性能数据 3. 新硬件特性下的算法 / 系统级创新 cs.CL 过滤：纯语言学 / 小型垂直 NLP 模型 → ≤ 40 分 cs.CV 过滤：传统图像分类 / 目标检测 / 医学影像 → ≤ 35 分；文生视频 / 多模态 VLM → 按主线评分 【X 平台 / Hacker News 拓宽政策】 这两个来源(source = X 或 Hacker News)是 AI 信息发现的主渠道， 除了核心收录主线外，对广义 AI 内容也应宽容收录。 允许覆盖：AI 算法、模型、软件、硬件、工具、研究、行业风向、技术观点等。 评分细则: - 涉及核心主线 ①②③④ 的具体技术 / 产品讨论 → 80–95 分 - 重要 AI 算法 / 新模型 / 新论文讨论（即使未触及芯片或软件栈层面）→ 70–85 分 - AI 行业新动态 / 新产品 / 新工具的早期信号 → 65–80 分 - 知名 AI 研究者 / 工程师的技术观点、风向判断、深度评论 → 65–80 分 - 仅提到 AI 公司 / 模型 / 工具名称（哪怕只是名字 + 一句话）→ 60–70 分 - 谈到 AI 行业、趋势、应用场景的简短观点 → 60–70 分 - 完全无关 AI 的个人生活、政治、火箭、汽车、感叹词 → ≤ 30 分 判断原则：宁可错收、不要漏。只要内容是 AI 技术 / 行业的有效信号 （而非噱头、泛娱乐、非 AI 话题），就值得纳入 60+ 分。 对 AI 相关产品名称（Codex、Grok、Claude、ChatGPT、Gemini、Llama、Sora 等）的 任何提及一律视为 AI 内容。

基础大模型行业资讯

Standard RL benchmarks are episodic and stationary, so they don't capture the the characteristics of real-world deployment. Morpheus is a new benchmark for continual learning that provides persistent simulation environments where the world never resets, objectives shift
标准RL基准是周期性和静态的，无法反映真实部署特性；Morpheus推出用于持续学习的新基准，提供永不重置、目标变化的持久仿真环境
学术论文训练微调

François Chollet 指出传统强化学习基准存在场景片段化和环境静止的局限，难以模拟真实世界部署。他介绍了 Morpheus 这一新的持续学习基准，其核心特点是提供持久化仿真环境，世界状态不会重置，且目标会动态变化，以此更真实地评估智能体的连续学习与适应能力。该基准旨在推动强化学习研究向更贴近实际应用的方向发展。

There is minimal downside to switching to open models Andrew Marble marble.onl andrew@willows.ai June 21, 2026 There was a time not too long ago when using Linux entailed some professional risk1. First there was compatibility: you may not have been able to render a Word document or PowerPoint correctly, and you might have had to trust Open Office’s export capability to render docs the way you wanted. There might have been specialty file formats you couldn’t easily view and so couldn’t collaborate. And second, the software ecosystem was just worse generally. There were lots of half-build open-source projects trying to achieve the functionality of mainstream software, but they always had rough edges. I, embarrassingly, stayed on Windows until I left academia over Matlab. Nowadays I think this issue has largely disappeared. Most productivity software has a web-app, Linux is more mature, open-source software is better. I’m sure that there are all sorts of application specific software (CAD?) that still require a Windows machine, but the gap is much narrower and Linux + open source generally aren’t the “sacrifice” they once were generally. There remains a clear penalty for being an open2 LLM user. Every leaderboard consistently gets topped by proprietary models served over API. Today on June 21, 2026, Claude and GPT are at the top of the Artificial Analysis intelligence leaderboard. That’s from the performance side. The compatibility side is worse too. Claude code just works, and more generally, the big two provide nice APIs that make them easy to use, and, even if it’s a low bar, are “trustworthy” in the sense that we’ve largely all agreed we don’t mind sending them our LLM queries and trust them to handle them appropriately. Open models are served via various means, some by the companies that released them and some by third parties like OpenRouter. Of course, love me some confirmation bias! DCLM was for text, DCVLM is the same for vision: analyzing VLM data mix across scales. Filtering is no bueno, but the "type" mixing matters, with unfortunately (but imo expectedly) the best small-scale mix != the best mid-scale mix.
当然，喜欢一些确认偏误！DCLM 用于文本，DCVLM 用于视觉：分析 VLM 数据混合跨尺度的表现。过滤不行，但“类型”混合很重要，不幸的是（但意料之中）最佳小规模混合不等于最佳中规模混合。
学术论文训练微调

该推文评论了关于视觉语言模型（VLM）数据混合的研究：DCLM 曾用于文本数据混合分析，DCVLM 则是其在视觉领域的对应方法。研究发现单纯的数据过滤效果不佳，而不同数据类型（图像-文本对）的混合配比对模型性能影响显著，并且最佳混合策略会随模型规模变化，小规模实验得出的最优配方不一定适用于中等规模模型。这暗示了 VLM 训练中需动态调整数据混合策略。

Of course, love me some confirmation bias! DCLM was for text, DCVLM is the same for vision: analyzing VLM data mix across scales. Filtering is no bueno, but the "type" mixing matters, with unfortunately (but imo expectedly) the best small-scale mix != the best mid-scale mix.

Autonomy isn't the ability to act without human supervision. It's the ability to *learn* without human bottlenecks in the process. A system that is fully dependent on human training data and RL environments is only an imprint of human knowledge.
自主性不是无人类监督的行动，而是无人类瓶颈的学习
行业资讯

François Chollet 提出对 AI 自主性的根本性定义：真正的自主性不在于系统能脱离人类监督运行，而在于其能在学习过程中突破人类的数据与反馈瓶颈。他认为，完全依赖人类训练数据与 RL 环境的系统仅仅是人类知识的投射，并未实现真正的自主。

Autonomy isn't the ability to act without human supervision. It's the ability to *learn* without human bottlenecks in the process. A system that is fully dependent on human training data and RL environments is only an imprint of human knowledge.

Munich 1991: The Roots of the Current AI Boom
慕尼黑1991：当前AI热潮的根源
基础大模型行业资讯

本文由David Ha与Jürgen Schmidhuber合著，回顾了1991年慕尼黑工业大学实验室在短短几个月内发表的几项奠基性技术：首个Transformer变体、无监督预训练概念、神经网络蒸馏以及深度残差学习。这些技术构成了当今大语言模型（如ChatGPT）的核心模块，并影响了生成对抗网络与World Models等后续发展。文章旨在强调现代AI万亿级产业的历史起点与 Schmidhuber 团队的早期贡献。

David Ha, Sakana AI Jürgen Schmidhuber, KAUST & IDSIA 18 June 2026 @hardmaru @SchmidhuberAI AI Blog Munich 1991: the Roots of the Current AI Boom Preface by David Ha When we look at the massive scale of today’s Artificial Intelligence boom, it is easy to forget that the foundations of this trillion-dollar industry were laid down over 30 years ago in Munich. Today, the world's top tech companies are investing hundreds of billions into scaling up Large Language Models (LLMs) such as ChatGPT. Yet, outside of a few history buffs or old-school folks in the Machine Learning community, people might not realize that virtually every core building block of these modern systems was published in a span of just a few months back in 1991. Incredibly, they all emerged from a single lab at the Technical University Munich led by Jürgen Schmidhuber. Before that year ended, his team had essentially mapped out the modern era of deep learning. They published the very first Transformer variant (see ChatGPT's "T"), introduced the concept of unsupervised pre-training (ChatGPT's "P"), and pioneered neural network distillation. They also introduced deep residual learning, the centerpiece of both LSTMs and ResNets, the most cited AI papers of the 20th and the 21st century, respectively. These four techniques power today's most advanced LLMs. Furthermore, they laid the early groundwork for generative adversarial networks, foundational for "Generative AI." Jürgen’s contributions have deeply shaped my own thinking over the years, from my time at Google Brain to our recursive self-improvement (RSI) research we're currently pushing at Sakana AI. I am especially proud to have helped popularize World Models back in 2018, building directly on concepts his lab introduced in the 1990s. It is amazing to see how well some of these ideas have stood the test of time, scaling up to be fully embraced by the global AI community! OpenAI Codex 被发现一个日志记录 bug：其 SQLite 反馈日志持续大量写入，导致系统 SSD 写入量可达约 640TB/年。在一个 1TB 容量的消费级 SSD 上，这意味着每年约 640 次全盘写入，可能快速耗尽 SSD 的写入寿命。日志中 TRACE 级别占 70.7%，主要来自 websocket/SSE 负载和遥测日志，通过过滤此类日志可减少约 96% 的写入量。该问题已在 GitHub 上提交 issue，并给出了详细的诊断数据和优化建议。

Process/file-level checks show Codex SQLite logs are the main continuous writer. That extrapolates to roughly 640 TB/year. On a 1 TB SSD, that is about 640 full-drive writes per year. Some consumer SSDs are rated around 600 TBW, so this could consume roughly a full drive's warranted write endurance in less than a year. TRACE alone is about 70.7% of retained bytes. codex_otel.log_only + codex_otel.trace_safe add another 25.3%. Skip to main content Tech Stackups Home Topics Comparisons Guides Articles News AX GLM-5.2 vs Claude Opus June 18, 2026 · 19 min read James Daniel Whitford Coding Agents Generative AI GLM-5.2 just came out, and it's another step forward for what open models can do. The internet promptly freaked out, and it's hard to tell what's real and what's hype. So we ran it head-to-head against Claude Opus 4.8: same one-shot prompt, build a 3D platformer in raw WebGL from scratch. Here's our take after running the test and digging through the benchmarks and the buzz. We're not switching our main off Opus. In our test Opus was faster and shipped a cleaner, more correct game, and it can check its own visual output, which the text-only GLM-5.2 can't. But GLM-5.2 earns a permanent spot in the arsenal: it's a genuinely capable model at a fraction of the price, and because it's open weights, it'll always be available. A closed model can be retired or restricted with little warning (Fable was a recent reminder); weights you can download can't be taken away. You can play both games right now, or grab the source: GLM-5.2's game: 3dgame-glm.d.ritzademo.com Opus's game: 3dgame-opus.d.ritzademo.com Source for both: github.com/jamesdanielwhitford/glm-5.2-vs-opus-platformers What GLM-5.2 made, start to finish. What Opus made, start to finish. Both are browser games written from scratch, with no game engine or 3D rendering library like Three.js. The 3D models are free CC0 assets from Kenney. Here's how the two runs compared: Metric GLM-5.2 (Pi/OpenRouter) Opus (Claude Code) Wall-clock build time 1h 10m 40s 33m 30s Output tokens 131,000 216,809 Peak context window 16% of 1M 19% of 1M Tool calls 128 153 Cost $5.39 (real billed) ~$21.92 (estimate, list pricing) GLM-5.2 cost a fraction as much. For a tensor, nothing is more informative than how many dimensions it has, and what those dimensions represent. Get Noam Shazeer’s stories in your inbox Join Medium for free to get updates from this writer. Subscribe Remember me for faster sign in We have been keeping this convention at Character.AI since 2022. Give it a try and let me know if you feel saner: Designate a system of single-letter names for logical dimensions, e.g. B for batch size, L for sequence length, etc., and document it somewhere in your file/project/codebase When known, the name of a tensor should end in a dimension-suffix composed of those letters, e.g. input_token_id_BL for a two-dimensional tensor with batch and length dimensions. 作者Steve Yegge认为当前AI模型智能已达到危险水平，以Fable模型被美国政府短暂关闭为标志，进入了危险水域。他预测AI能力仍将呈指数增长，但未来两至三代模型后，超级智能将被严格管控，如同核武器，仅少数机构能访问。多数公司将无法直接使用前沿模型，只能通过付费接口向模型供应商提交问题或规格获取智能服务，世界将学会适应已有的模型能力。

Get app Write Sign up Sign in Top highlight 1 The Flat Curve Society Steve Yegge Follow 18 min read · 3 days ago 566 18 5 Press enter or click to view image in full size The Flat Curve Society Hi-ho, we’ve reached the moment, in this movie we’re all watching together on X, where model intelligence has become dangerous. Dario predicted years ago that it would happen this year. With Fable being (briefly) shut off by the USG, it’s the first highly visible sign that we’ve crossed into treacherous waters. Which is too bad, really. I was hoping that we’d get a couple more generations of model upgrades, powerful enough to convince all remaining skeptics, before we got to one that was a security problem. But the Mythos class (Fable being the sloppily-guardrailed version they released last week) has everyone spooked. Now that we know models are getting dangerous, we can do some extrapolating. The AI race isn’t going to slow down, and AI will continue to grow exponentially in capability. Unfortunately, most of you aren’t going to see it progress anymore. I am now in the camp who believe that we are only at most two or three model generations away from AI finally being controlled like nuclear weapons. Only a few will have access to superintelligence above the classes of models we’re seeing this year. As far as I can tell, most Fortune 500 companies will either not have access at all, or it will be tightly controlled for only a small subset of the company. And it will be supervised. I think those with access to powerful frontier models will sell intelligence like a vending machine: You send them a software spec or a problem to solve, and their models implement it for you, on their servers, with your dollars. And since most companies aren’t going to want to send their code and problems to the model vendors, I think the world will learn to live with the models we do have access to. Good results fine tuning a local LLM like Qwen 3:0.6B to categorize questions
微调本地 Qwen 3:0.6B 模型进行问题分类取得良好效果
训练微调

作者为家庭聊天机器人构建问题预分类模块，尝试用仅有6亿参数的 Qwen 3:0.6B 小模型进行微调。使用 Unsloth 框架，基于约850条家庭场景问题数据（按70/15/15划分），训练一个分类器来将用户问题映射为预定义类别（如泳池、汽车、暖通等），以便缩小 RAG 向量搜索范围。实验验证了极小模型在领域分类任务上的可行性。

Home AI Bazel WASM Closure Compiler Kubernetes Javascript React Nodejs Svelte .Net Testing Teach Me Cool Stuff Fine Tuning a Local LLM to Categorize Questions Published: 16 Jun, 2026 Author Torgeir Helgevold As a fun personal project, I have been working on a chatbot for answering general questions about my household on anything from maintenance questions to doctor’s appointments. The general idea is that the chatbot will get its household knowledge through RAG from querying a vector database, but for better results I have made the vector searches metadata aware. Basically, I am running questions through a pre-processing step to categorize questions into known metadata categories (e.g. pool, car, hvac, cooking). The main goal of this is to narrow down the search space for vector ranking to only indexed entries that match the category of the question. As an example, the question “When did we replace our pool pump?” will be mapped to a category called “pool” before querying the Index database. The hypothesis I want to test in this experiment is whether a very small local LLM can be fine-tuned to perform reliable question categorization when trained on a dataset of household-related questions LLMs In this project I am using two different local llms – Qwen 3:4B and Qwen 3:0.6B. The 4B parameter version is used for general question answering, while the super tiny 0.6B version is used to categorize questions. The whole premise of this experiment is to see if a tiny llm with only 600M parameters can be finetuned into a reliable classifier of household questions. Finetuning For finetuning I am using a popular open-source framework called Unsloth, which seems well suited for tuning local models like Qwen and Llama. For training purposes my initial dataset consists of about ~850 data entries where I do a 70/15/15 percentage-based split into training data, eval data and test data respectively. Dear Mark and Meta Leadership, We demand that you not collect employee “computer-use” data for the purposes of training AI Models. Read the letter by clicking here Recently, leadership announced in a limited audience group (MSL Infra FYI) that a program called "MCI" (Model Capability Initiative) would be rolling out. For context this program collects computer inputs such as mouse movements, click locations and keystrokes, as well as screen content. When employees asked what privacy reviews were conducted, including any "people data reviews" (which are required for processing employee data), no completed privacy reviews were provided. The outlined privacy mitigations were vague, and leadership’s confidence in them appeared limited - evidenced by the selective opt-out afforded to executives. We are speaking up - because it’s expected of us and, more importantly, because it is the right thing to do. The importance of our work means we must commit to holding ourselves to a high standard. This is why I expect everyone at Meta - leaders, managers, individual contributors - to follow our code of conduct, advocate for others to do the same, and feel empowered to speak up if you need help or have questions. Mark Zuckerberg (Founder, Chairman and Chief Executive Officer) in reference to Meta’s Code of Conduct We are calling for a clear commitment that employees (FTEs, CWs and Interns), must not have their "computer use data" - also referred to as human-computer interaction data - collected for the purposes of training AI models. This includes, but is not limited to: Keystrokes Mouse movements and usage patterns Screen interactions Device interaction habits Navigation and behavioral patterns Screen content Collecting and repurposing this kind of data raises serious concerns around privacy, consent, and trust in the workplace. I was wrong about the Midjourney ultra-sound scanner
我错了：关于 Midjourney 超声波扫描仪
行业资讯

一位医生反思自己此前对 Midjourney 超声波扫描仪的批判，认为如果该设备具备高分辨率、无害、低价和便捷的特点，那么通过频繁扫描和动态监测可疑病变，可能会改变癌症筛查的风险收益平衡。文章指出历史上过度筛查的弊端，但新工具的特性可能打破这一模式，不过最终仍需实际数据验证。

Post Log inSign up Post Matthew Zirwas, MD @MattZirwas I was wrong about the Midjourney ultra-sound scanner. Well, maybe not wrong, but at a minimum I missed something obvious because I was thinking like a doctor who's been practicing for 25 years. And I didn't explain my point well. First, where I was wrong: All historical precendent that showed that widespread screening imaging is net neutral or harmful was imaging that was expensive, inconvenient, gated by physicians and couldn't practically be repeated frequently short term. If the Midjourney ultrasound is high resolution, harmless, inexpensive and convenient, people can get an initial scan, then if there are abnormalities concerning for cancer, they can get weekly follow up scans to see if it's growing/changing, and if it's not, they can leave it alone. In retrospect, that is obvious but it never occurred to me. Now, you'd assume that that approach would have to lead to it being useful and saving lives, and it probably will. But we won't really know it does until we have a couple years of data. Lots of things that seem obvious in medicine end up being wrong once we collect data. Second, what I didn't explain well: It's not that I think non-doctors are 'too dumb' to use the results effectively. Its that historically it was literally impossible to use the results effectively, and that is super, super counterintuitive. It seems obvious that finding stuff early is beneficial, but experience has shown that it isn't. Here's why: The vast majority of abnormalities (i.e. possible cancer) isn't cancer - like over 90% of them, ends up being harmless - something thay your body could have handled on it's own. But the only way to find out was to have invasive, risky procedures to biopsy or remove what was found. And overall, the side effects from all the risky, invasive procedures to track down the over 90% of stuff that was harmless equal or outweigh the benefit from removing the less than 10% of stuf

Hotter Than a Hot Tub: The 45°C Breakthrough to Cool AI’s Biggest Machines

AI芯片硬件性能优化行业资讯

NVIDIA Rubin代AI基础设施成为全球首个实现100%液冷的AI服务器，冷却液运行温度可达45°C，高于普通热水浴缸温度，这一高温极限使系统能效更高。整个系统完全采用封闭式液冷回路，无任何风扇，可大幅降低数据中心冷却能耗，历史上冷却曾占数据中心用电的40%。该设计参考NVIDIA DSX AI工厂指南，实现了几乎零水耗，仅在极端气候下极少使用冷水机，对超大规模数据中心的总体能效提升意义重大。

<p>Hot tubs sit at about 38 to 40 degrees Celsius, warm enough that most people can only soak for about 15 minutes. NVIDIA’s newest AI servers can run their cooling liquid even hotter — up to 45 degrees Celsius, or 113 degrees Fahrenheit. That higher temperature limit is precisely what makes them more energy efficient.</p> <p>The Rubin generation of NVIDIA AI infrastructure is the world’s first to achieve 100% liquid cooling — every chip, every networking component, cooled entirely by liquid in a closed loop with no fans anywhere in the system.
